system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:49:22 UTC, the domain controller recorded a service-ticket event for svc-archive requesting access to FILE-NWD-01 from 139.162.174.124, a public IP address. This is inconsistent with the supplied context that there is no VPN and remote administration is only performed from WS-SOKAFOR-01; it is a strong indicator of suspicious external credential use, though it does not by itself establish a successful logon.

At 13:50:07 UTC, FILE-NWD-01 sent 640,000,237 bytes to PROXY-NWD-01 on port 8080. This confirms a large transfer to the proxy, but the record does not identify the external destination or establish that the bytes left the organization.

At 14:14:37 UTC, PROXY-NWD-01 initiated an RDP connection to FILE-NWD-01; the corresponding FILE-NWD-01 event records a failed logon attempt for svc_mgmt with status indicating the account is disabled. This is suspicious given the supplied policy that remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01.
At 14:14:39 UTC, FILE-NWD-01 connected to PROXY-NWD-01 over SSH, a service not listed as approved in the supplied environment context.
Immediately after the SSH connection, FILE-NWD-01 made an SMB connection to DC-NWD-01; the domain controller recorded a failed NTLM logon attempt for disabled account svc_mgmt from FILE-NWD-01.

known_telemetry_limitations: FILE-NWD-01 winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, leaving a gap in endpoint process, logon, and related event evidence during the large transfer.
PROXY-NWD-01 proxy-log collection was unavailable from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so the proxy-side request details and external destination associated with the large transfer are unavailable.
The available Zeek record for the large transfer identifies FILE-NWD-01, the proxy address, port 8080, and byte counts, but not the process responsible or the ultimate destination.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish that the 640 MB transfer reached an external destination, what its destination was, or what data it contained.
The evidence does not attribute the large transfer to the approved StratoSafe backup agent or establish that it was a backup upload.
The svc-archive service-ticket event does not, by itself, establish a successful interactive or service logon, or prove who controlled the source IP.
The evidence does not establish the cause or operator of the RDP, SSH, or SMB activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain proxy logs, including CONNECT/request destination, authenticated user, and byte counts for FILE-NWD-01 during 13:30–14:10 UTC.
Collect FILE-NWD-01 endpoint process, service, scheduled-task, logon, and network telemetry for the collection-outage interval; specifically identify the process responsible for the 640 MB transfer.
Review domain-controller authentication details and surrounding records for svc-archive, including whether the ticket was used and whether the external source IP is known or authorized.
Verify the svc-render password rotation and manual job update, and inspect relevant service-account and backup-agent configuration and execution records.
Preserve and investigate FILE-NWD-01 and PROXY-NWD-01 for the RDP, SSH, and disabled svc_mgmt logon attempts, including account status, process evidence, and any related activity.
